hints: Notice the doorway width is $0.80 \text{ m}$ - significant diffraction occurs when the wavelength is close to the gap width.
Use $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to link each given frequency to its wavelength, so lower frequency means larger wavelength.
Calculate $\lambda = 340/f$ for the $10^{2} \text{ Hz}$ options and check which wavelength is closest to $0.80 \text{ m}$.
walkthrough: Identify the condition for maximum diffraction: spreading is greatest when wavelength $\lambda$ is approximately equal to the gap width, here $0.80 \text{ m}$.
State the wave equation for sound in air: $v = f\lambda$, so $\lambda = v/f$ with $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Check the two realistic audio frequencies: for $2.7 \times 10^{2} \text{ Hz}$, $\lambda = 340/270 \approx 1.26 \text{ m}$.
Compare with the gap: $0.79 \text{ m}$ is almost exactly $0.80 \text{ m}$, while $1.26 \text{ m}$ and the huge wavelengths from options A and B are much further away.
Therefore the $4.3 \times 10^{2} \text{ Hz}$ wave has $\lambda$ closest to the doorway width and diffracts the most. This is option D.

options.A: With $f = 2.4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ Hz}$, $\lambda = v/f$ is about $1.4 \times 10^{5} \text{ m}$, far larger than the $0.80 \text{ m}$ gap and not the closest match for maximum diffraction.
options.B: With $f = 8.0 \times 10^{-1} \text{ Hz}$, $\lambda = v/f$ is about $425 \text{ m}$, far larger than the $0.80 \text{ m}$ gap and not the closest match for maximum diffraction.
options.C: With $f = 2.7 \times 10^{2} \text{ Hz}$, $\lambda = v/f$ is about $1.3 \text{ m}$, larger than the $0.80 \text{ m}$ gap and further from the gap width than option D.
options.D: With $f = 4.3 \times 10^{2} \text{ Hz}$, $\lambda = v/f$ is about $0.79 \text{ m}$, almost equal to the $0.80 \text{ m}$ doorway, giving the greatest diffraction.
